title: A data-driven approach for systematic correction of electronic bandgaps
title_zh: 电子带隙系统校正的数据驱动方法
summary: 我们证明，将单个机器学习校正应用于使用两种最常用的能量泛函的密度泛函理论计算的带隙，会产生接近实验值的带隙。这解决了计算高效的电子结构方法的经典问题，给出了可以与实验进行比较的可靠带隙。所采用的方法依赖于机器学习模型的材料特定特征工程，并且被证明与基于 GW 近似或混合泛函的更昂贵的计算具有接近的准确性。这里报告的研究结果开启了在需要可靠带隙的材料设计工作流程中使用高效计算的可能性，这对针对大型计算数据库的研究或本质上完全预测的研究具有影响。
abstract: arXiv:2611.10889v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We demonstrate that a single machine-learning correction, applied to bandgaps from density functional theory calculations with two of the most frequently used energy functionals, results in bandgaps that are close to the experimental values. This solves a classical problem of computationally efficient electronic structure methods, to give reliable bandgaps that can be compared to experiments. The employed approach relies on materials specific feature engineering of machine learning models, and is shown to have close accuracy to that of much more expensive calculations based on the GW-approximation or hybrid functionals. The findings reported here open the possibility to use efficient calculations in materials design workflows that need reliable bandgaps, with implications for investigations targeting large computational databases or for investigations that are entirely predictive in nature.

title: MCSA: Multi-Cutoff Spectral Aggregation in SO(3) Equivariant GNNs for Interatomic Potentials
title_zh: 文献研究：MCSA: Multi-Cutoff Spectral Aggregation in SO(3) Equivariant GNNs for Interatomic Potentials
summary: Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials (MLIPs) based on Equivariant Graph Neural Networks (EGNNs) have achieved remarkable progress in atomistic modeling. However, accurately representing atomic inte…
abstract: arXiv:2611.11226v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials (MLIPs) based on Equivariant Graph Neural Networks (EGNNs) have achieved remarkable progress in atomistic modeling. However, accurately representing atomic interactions across different spatial scales remains challenging. In this work, we investigate the radial spectral properties of SO(3)-equivariant message passing and establish that the cutoff radius controls the characteristic spatial-frequency scale of radial interactions. Based on this analysis, we propose Multi-Cutoff Spectral Aggregation (MCSA), a plug-and-play module that aggregates radial kernels with different cutoff radii to enrich multi-scale geometric representations. To achieve efficient implementation, we exploit the compact support of radial kernels to fuse cutoff-dependent radial weights before angular tensor-product operations, avoiding redundant angular computations while preserving rotational equivariance. Extensive experiments across representative EGNN backbones demonstrate consistent improvements in energy, force, and stress prediction, as well as enhanced accuracy in higher-order properties, including phonon dispersion and lattice thermal conductivity. Further evaluations on layered materials with distinct interaction scales demonstrate the effectiveness of physically motivated cutoff selection. Code is available at: https://github.com/JF-Tan/MCSA.

title: Defects and Structural Evolution in CrSBr: Machine-Learning Potentials for Atomistic Simulations
title_zh: 文献研究：Defects and Structural Evolution in CrSBr: Machine-Learning Potentials for Atomistic Simulations
summary: The layered van der Waals semiconductor CrSBr combines intrinsic magnetic order with semiconducting and optical properties, making it a promising material for multifunctional electronic and photonic a…
abstract: arXiv:2611.12267v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The layered van der Waals semiconductor CrSBr combines intrinsic magnetic order with semiconducting and optical properties, making it a promising material for multifunctional electronic and photonic applications. Understanding how defects and structural transformations affect its properties under experimentally relevant conditions, however, remains challenging for first-principles simulations due to the relevant length and time scales. Here, we develop and benchmark machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) for the Cr-S-Br system, enabling large-scale atomistic simulations of CrSBr with accuracy approaching that of density functional theory (DFT). The charge-aware variant qNEP achieves near-DFT accuracy in predicting lattice constants, formation enthalpies, vacancy energetics, and the anisotropic pressure response of o-CrSBr. Nudged elastic band calculations reveal that pre-existing S vacancies lower the Cr Frenkel-pair migration barrier by up to 1.1 eV, providing an atomistic mechanism for beam-induced Cr redistribution and structural transformations. Displacement threshold calculations further show that Br is the most susceptible species to electron-beam-induced displacement, identifying the relative ease of removing different atomic species. Together, these results establish a validated computational framework for investigating atomic-scale disorder and structural transformations in CrSBr, providing a basis for defect engineering in materials for future magneto-optoelectronic applications.

title: AI-Driven Discovery of Entanglement Witness in Spin Hamiltonians
title_zh: 文献研究：AI-Driven Discovery of Entanglement Witness in Spin Hamiltonians
summary: Entanglement is a crucial resource in quantum science and engineering, but detecting it in many-body states from experimentally accessible observables remains challenging. Here we introduce EntNet, an…
abstract: arXiv:2611.11935v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Entanglement is a crucial resource in quantum science and engineering, but detecting it in many-body states from experimentally accessible observables remains challenging. Here we introduce EntNet, an AI-driven framework to discover compact combinations of spin observables that accurately distinguish entangled from fully separable many-body mixed states in one-dimensional spin-1/2 chains governed by short-range Hamiltonians. We construct local-unitary-invariant representations of measurable Pauli correlators up to four-body order, sparsely select 16 candidate invariant feature channels, and learn their spatial structure using a Transformer architecture with rotary positional embeddings. Using only expectation values of these low-order observables, EntNet achieves >98% recall on certified entangled states with near-zero false-positive rates on separable states. Remarkably, it exhibits transferability across system sizes and distinct Hamiltonian families, including frustrated and disordered spin models, with minimal loss of accuracy. Beyond detection, EntNet provides physical insight into entanglement detection by revealing a selective spatial organization of pair correlations, while its finite-temperature decision boundary tracks the excitation gap of Jordan-Wigner quasiparticles. These results establish a transferable and physically interpretable framework for data-driven discovery of entanglement witnesses from local correlation functions.

title: Experimentally Grounded Machine Learning of PrecursorSurface-Reactant Chemistry in Atomic Layer Deposition
title_zh: 文献研究：Experimentally Grounded Machine Learning of PrecursorSurface-Reactant Chemistry in Atomic Layer Deposition
summary: Whether a precursor-substrate-reactant combination yields an atomic layer deposition (ALD) process is still settled by trial-and-error experiments. Here we introduce AJIN (ALD Joint Interpretable Netw…
abstract: arXiv:2611.10024v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Whether a precursor-substrate-reactant combination yields an atomic layer deposition (ALD) process is still settled by trial-and-error experiments. Here we introduce AJIN (ALD Joint Interpretable Network), a machine-learning framework that learns this decision from experimental outcomes. We compiled 560 experimentally observed ALD and area-selective ALD outcomes spanning 76 precursors, 27 substrates, 20 reactants and 25-620 degrees Celsius. Following the ALD cycle, AJIN predicts adsorption from graph-neural-network embeddings of the precursor and substrate with temperature, and deposition by adding the reactant. The best model (CHGNet-MLP) reaches balanced accuracies of 79.2% for adsorption and 84.8% for deposition and transfers partially to unseen precursors. SHAP and ablation analyses show that substrate chemistry governs adsorption, whereas precursor, substrate and reactant all contribute to deposition. Tested against our laboratory's ALD experiments, AJIN correctly predicted 83% of new-substrate cases and 71% of new precursor-substrate adsorption cases, providing an experimentally grounded tool for prioritizing ALD and area-selective ALD chemistries.

title: Interpretable machine learning of formation energies and band gaps in hybrid perovskites through SHAP analysis and SISSO modelling
title_zh: 通过 SHAP 分析和 SISSO 建模对混合钙钛矿中的形成能和带隙进行可解释的机器学习
summary: 准确且可解释的性质预测对于探索有机-无机杂化钙钛矿至关重要。在这里，我们将机器学习筛选与 SHAP 分析和 SISSO 描述符发现相结合。使用 4,456 种化合物，优化的 XGBoost 模型在测试集上实现了形成能 R² 值为 0.99，带隙 R² 值为 0.93，并应用于超过 180,000 个候选化合物。
abstract: arXiv:2611.09944v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate and interpretable property prediction is essential for exploring hybrid organic-inorganic perovskites. Here, we combine machine-learning screening with SHAP analysis and SISSO descriptor discovery. Using 4,456 compounds, optimized XGBoost models achieved test-set R² values of 0.99 for formation energy and 0.93 for band gap and were applied to over 180,000 candidates. Comparison across approximately 17,000 common compounds revealed broadly overlapping distributions from XGBoost and CGCNN but substantially lower predictions from UPET, suggesting potential limitations in its transferability to hybrid organic-inorganic perovskites. SHAP analysis and correlation-based pruning retained eight primary features for each property, from which SISSO derived expressions comprising four nonlinear descriptors. These expressions couple molecular and inorganic properties for formation energy and emphasize relative atomic sizes and B-site characteristics for band gap. This framework supports efficient candidate prioritization and interpretable analysis of learned structures-property relationships in hybrid perovskites.

title: PBE-assisted machine learning of HSE06+SOC photovoltaic efficiency in halide perovskites
title_zh: 文献研究：PBE-assisted machine learning of HSE06+SOC photovoltaic efficiency in halide perovskites
summary: Hybrid-functional calculations with spin–orbit coupling (HSE06 + SOC) provide more accurate electronic properties of halide perovskites than semilocal PBE calculations but are substantially more expen…
abstract: Hybrid-functional calculations with spin–orbit coupling (HSE06 + SOC) provide more accurate electronic properties of halide perovskites than semilocal PBE calculations but are substantially more expensive. Here, we assess whether low-cost PBE information improves machine-learning (ML) prediction of HSE06 + SOC band gaps and spectroscopic limited maximum efficiency (SLME). Using a public dataset of 243 pure and mixed ABX₃ perovskites, we compare seven ML model families using nested cross-validation with random, chemical-system-grouped, and B-site-grouped splits. PBE inputs substantially improve SLME prediction: the mean absolute error decreases from 0.68 to 0.45 percentage points on chemical-system-grouped splits, with the best model achieving 0.36 percentage points. Δ-learning provides no advantage over direct learning. However, performance deteriorates when the B-site chemistry is absent from training, and conformal intervals become under-calibrated. An audit of the source labels further shows that the HSE06 + SOC SLME is strongly constrained by the HSE06 + SOC band gap and approaches a saturation near 16%, because the reported spectrum was generated by shifting the PBE absorption spectrum. These findings highlight both the value and limitations of PBE-assisted ML for multi-fidelity prediction of perovskite properties.

title: Machine Learning-Assisted Prediction of Brilliant Green Removal from Water Using CaTiO 3 Photocatalysis: Bayesian Optimization, SHAP Explainability, and Robustness Assessment
title_zh: 文献研究：Machine Learning-Assisted Prediction of Brilliant Green Removal from Water Using CaTiO 3 Photocatalysis: Bayesian Optimization, SHAP Explainability, and Robustness Assessment
summary: Brilliant Green (BG)-contaminated wastewater threatens aquatic ecosystems by limiting light penetration, disrupting photosynthesis, and exposing organisms to potentially toxic compounds, raising broad…
abstract: Brilliant Green (BG)-contaminated wastewater threatens aquatic ecosystems by limiting light penetration, disrupting photosynthesis, and exposing organisms to potentially toxic compounds, raising broader environmental and human-health concerns. This study presents an explainable machine-learning framework for predicting BG removal during CaTiO3-assisted photocatalytic water treatment. Using 63 published experimental observations for the 2:7 precursor composition, six regression models Decision Tree, Random Forest, Extra Trees, Gradient Boosting, XGBoost, and CatBoost were evaluated through Bayesian hyperparameter optimization and repeated cross-validation. Although Extra Trees achieved marginally higher holdout accuracy, CatBoost was selected for its superior repeated-validation performance, achieving a test R2 of 0.9884, RMSE of 3.4629 percentage points, and mean cross-validation R2 of 0.9697. SHAP analysis identified degradation time (60.57%), initial BG concentration (32.12%), and catalyst dosage (7.31%) as the principal contributors to model predictions. Feature-combination analysis reinforced this hierarchy, while CatBoost retained a test R2 of 0.9778 under 10% Gaussian noise. Predicted BG removal (89.32%) closely matched the reported experimental value (88.46%). These findings provide a promising foundation for future experimental validation, broader catalyst screening, and interpretable optimization of photocatalytic wastewater treatment.

title: FT-NIR Spectroscopy and Explainable Machine Learning for Eggshell Based Classification of Organic and Conventional Market Eggs
title_zh: FT-NIR 光谱和可解释的机器学习用于基于蛋壳的有机和传统市场鸡蛋分类
summary: 有机鸡蛋的溢价刺激了产品虚假陈述，并推动了快速、无损筛选工具的开发，以区分贴有标签的有机鸡蛋和传统鸡蛋。傅里叶变换近红外 (FT-NIR) 光谱与机器学习相结合，对销售的零售鸡蛋进行有机鸡蛋和传统鸡蛋的分类进行了评估。总共测量了 147 个鸡蛋，并使用偏最小二乘判别分析 (PLS-DA) 以及梯度增强树模型（XGBoost 和 LightGBM）对光谱进行了分析。数据集分为训练集 (70%) 和测试集 (30%)。
abstract: The premium pricing of organic eggs creates incentives for product misrepresentation and motivates the development of rapid, non-destructive screening tools to differentiate labeled organic and conventional eggs. Fourier transform near-infrared (FT-NIR) spectroscopy coupled with machine learning was evaluated for classifying retail eggs marketed as organic versus conventional. A total of 147 eggs were measured and spectra were analyzed using partial least squares–discriminant analysis (PLS-DA), along with gradient-boosted tree models (XGBoost and LightGBM). The dataset was partitioned into training (70%) and testing (30%) sets. Among the evaluated models, PLS-DA achieved the best test performance with an overall accuracy of 91.0%. To improve interpretability, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were used to identify wavelengths that most strongly contributed to model predictions. Influential regions included bands near ~1400 nm, consistent with O-H absorptions commonly associated with moisture-related spectral features, and regions near ~2300 nm, which are often associated with crystalline calcium-carbonate-related absorptions in the near-infrared and may reflect variation in mineral-associated spectral response of eggshell. These results indicate that FT-NIR spectroscopy combined with machine learning can differentiate retail eggs labeled as organic versus conventional under the conditions of this study, supporting further development of rapid screening approaches for market classification and quality assurance applications.

title: Out-of-the-Box Tabular Foundation Models for Bayesian Optimization in Materials Discovery
title_zh: 文献研究：Out-of-the-Box Tabular Foundation Models for Bayesian Optimization in Materials Discovery
summary: Bayesian optimization is widely used in active learning loops for materials science. Gaussian processes serve as the de-facto surrogate model family, but require task-dependent kernel choices and can…
abstract: arXiv:2611.12491v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Bayesian optimization is widely used in active learning loops for materials science. Gaussian processes serve as the de-facto surrogate model family, but require task-dependent kernel choices and can lack the modeling capacity for complex relationships. Tabular foundation models (TFMs) have recently emerged as the state-of-the-art for predictive tasks on structured data, without requiring bespoke kernels or hyperparameter tuning. We evaluate two TFMs, TabPFN and TabICL, as out-of-the-box surrogate models on two standard materials science benchmarks, comparing against a large field of baselines encompassing Gaussian processes, random forests, and CatBoost. Our findings indicate that TFMs are highly competitive surrogate models across the two benchmarks, without task-specific training for active learning or GP kernel selection. Our results motivate developing TFMs further as surrogates for active learning in materials discovery.

title: Ab Initio Molecular Dynamics-Guided Machine-Learning Potentials for Mapping Nitric Oxide Interactions with Oxygen-Covered Graphite
title_zh: 文献研究：Ab Initio Molecular Dynamics-Guided Machine-Learning Potentials for Mapping Nitric Oxide Interactions with Oxygen-Covered Graphite
summary: Exploratory ab initio molecular dynamics is used to construct machine-learning interatomic potentials for NO interactions with highly oriented pyrolytic graphite at 33% bridge-site oxygen coverage. Re…
abstract: arXiv:2611.12573v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Exploratory ab initio molecular dynamics is used to construct machine-learning interatomic potentials for NO interactions with highly oriented pyrolytic graphite at 33% bridge-site oxygen coverage. Representative configurations sampled across surface temperatures and incidence energies provide reference energies and forces for training and validation. The selected potential enables relaxation of 300 adsorption configurations and construction of spatial and angular interaction maps. These maps reveal increasingly restricted attractive regions during vertical approach and reduced short-range repulsion upon molecular reorientation. The resulting adsorption geometries and interaction landscapes guide further first-principles sampling toward refining potentials for NO oxidation dynamics.

title: Topological Deep Learning Challenge 2026: Bridging the Gap
title_zh: 文献研究：Topological Deep Learning Challenge 2026: Bridging the Gap
summary: This paper describes the 2026 edition of the Topological Deep Learning Challenge: Bridging the Gap, hosted at the second Topology, Algebra, and Geometry in Data Science (TAG-DS) Conference. Where prev…
abstract: arXiv:2611.10046v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper describes the 2026 edition of the Topological Deep Learning Challenge: Bridging the Gap, hosted at the second Topology, Algebra, and Geometry in Data Science (TAG-DS) Conference. Where previous editions grew the modelling and data ecosystem of Topological Deep Learning (TDL), this edition set out to place Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) and Topological Neural Networks (TNNs) side by side under a single evaluation pipeline. Participants implemented recent state-of-the-art architectures in TopoBench, with Track 1 covering GNNs and Track 2 covering TNNs. They evaluated these implementations on shared synthetic benchmarks generated with GraphUniverse, which independently controls homophily, average degree and degree-distribution heaviness. The challenge yielded 68 qualifying submissions from 34 teams, spanning the graph, simplicial, cellular, hypergraph and combinatorial domains. For the first time, submissions were also tracked on a public leaderboard, which we summarize and analyze here. Our analysis finds that the differences between the submitted tracks are strongly task-dependent: the mean accuracy gap is modest on community detection, while on triangle counting the Track 1 mean error is 1.85 times the Track 2 mean. Several structurally informed GNNs also outperform the Track 2 mean on triangle counting.

title: A Differentiable DFT-Based Framework for Inverse Materials Design
title_zh: 文献研究：A Differentiable DFT-Based Framework for Inverse Materials Design
summary: Discovering solid-state materials with target properties remains a central challenge in computational materials science. Existing data-driven approaches rely on training data and may generalize poorly…
abstract: arXiv:2606.25502v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Discovering solid-state materials with target properties remains a central challenge in computational materials science. Existing data-driven approaches rely on training data and may generalize poorly outside the training distribution. Here we develop a first-principles inverse-design framework that requires no training data. It integrates reverse-mode automatic differentiation (AD) into the Korringa--Kohn--Rostoker method combined with the coherent potential approximation (KKR-CPA), in which elemental concentrations serve as continuous optimization variables. Reverse-mode AD computes all concentration gradients in one backward pass, enabling optimization over dozens of candidate elements. Any differentiable quantity computable within KKR-CPA can serve as an optimization objective. We demonstrate this generality in permanent-magnet and half-metal design, identifying candidates such as (Nd₀.₉₈₃Pr₀.₀₁₇)(Co₀.₇₂Fe₀.₂₈)₂Fe₃ and FeMn(As₀.₈₃P₀.₁₇), respectively. We also synthesized materials with five SmCo₅-based compositions selected during optimization for higher magnetization. Their measured magnetization agreed closely with calculated values. Our framework offers a first-principles route to designing materials with target properties.

title: Engineering ferroelectric nanocapacitors through interfacial phonon bias
title_zh: 通过界面声子偏置设计铁电纳米电容器
summary: 随着铁电器件接近纳米尺度，它们的行为对边界条件变得越来越敏感。在钙钛矿氧化物纳米电容器中，外延应变和静电屏蔽是公认的控制参数。然后，虽然预计有助于铁电超薄膜的外延稳定，但电极的晶格动力学状态尚未被隔离为独立的调谐旋钮。在这里，我们将这种探索不足的耦合界面声子偏置称为耦合界面声子偏置，电极的声子能量景观通过其共享界面重塑相邻铁电体的声子能量景观。利用第一原理精确的机器学习原子间势和分子动力学模拟，我们研究了与金属钙钛矿氧化物接触的对称 BiFeO{}₃ 纳米电容器中的这种机制。
abstract: arXiv:2611.11256v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As ferroelectric devices approach the nanometer scale, their behavior becomes increasingly sensitive to boundary conditions. In perovskite oxide nanocapacitors, epitaxial strain and electrostatic screening are well-established control parameters. Then, while expected to contribute to the epitaxial stabilization of ferroelectric ultrathin films, the lattice-dynamical state of the electrodes has not been isolated as an independent tuning knob. Here we call this poorly explored coupling interfacial phonon bias, whereby the electrodes' phonon energy landscape reshapes that of the adjacent ferroelectric across their shared interface. Using first-principles-accurate machine-learned interatomic potentials and molecular-dynamics simulations, we examine this mechanism in symmetric BiFeO{}₃ nanocapacitors in contact with a metallic perovskite oxide. By independently controlling the orientatio and amplitude of the electrodes' octahedral-tilt landscape, while keeping conventional elastic and electric boundary conditions fixed, we show that the electrodes' phonon energy landscape can modify the stability of competing BiFeO{}₃ phases. In particular, this allows us to shift the ferroelectric transition temperature and even induce antiferroelectric-like switching at ambient conditions. We thus showcase interfacial phonon bias as a complementary and powerful strategy to modify and optimize the properties of ultrathin epitaxial films.

title: Overcoming speed-accuracy trade-offs with medium-sized interatomic potentials
title_zh: 克服中等原子间势的速度与精度的权衡
summary: 当前的机器学习原子间势提供了小型、快速模型和大型、富有表现力的网络之间的选择。这项研究展示了中间势如何以最便宜的现有形式主义为代价接近可转移精度的极限。具体来说，我们使用原子团簇展开对含氦 W-Ta-Hf-Cr-V-Ti 合金进行建模，该原子团簇展开将每个多项式的径向分量学习为独立的线性变换，并使用学习的指数嵌入大量密度。虽然（接近）训练损失很大程度上取决于模型大小，但不同验证集上的误差接近于参数多十倍的领先潜力的误差。
abstract: arXiv:2611.11544v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Current machine-learned interatomic potentials offer a choice between small, fast models and large, expressive networks. This study demonstrates how an intermediate potential can approach the limit of transferable accuracy at the cost of the cheapest existing formalisms. Specifically, we model He-bearing W-Ta-Hf-Cr-V-Ti alloys with an atomic cluster expansion that learns the radial components of each polynomial as independent linear transforms and embeds numerous densities with learned exponents. While (near-)training loss appears largely a function of model size, the error on a distinct validation set is close to that of leading potentials with ten times more parameters. Taking advantage of the new structure, we develop optimized implementations that run more than an order of magnitude faster than the larger models and many times faster than smaller models with equivalent polynomials. The potential is trained on systematically enumerated small structures but generalizes to point and planar defects and can be extended to even more complex chemistries. As a demonstration, we simulate radiation-damage cascades in billion-atom systems for hundreds of thousands of timesteps.

title: Learning Electronic Band Structures Across the s, p, d Blocks with an Empirical Pseudopotential Network
title_zh: 使用经验赝势网络学习跨 s、p、d 块的电子能带结构
summary: 电子能带结构控制晶体传导电子和吸收光的方式。密度泛函理论 (DFT) 通过成本高昂的自洽迭代来计算它们，而现有的机器学习模型要么预测孤立的标量属性，要么输出仍需要 DFT 求解器的哈密顿量。在这里，我们提出了 EpNet，这是一种学习的晶体经验赝势，跨越 s、p 和 d 块的 63 个元素。等变神经网络根据物理驱动的局部势和非局部投影构建其哈密顿量。 EpNet 仅根据能带能量进行训练，直接从原子坐标预测完整的能带结构。
abstract: arXiv:2611.11070v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electronic band structures govern how crystals conduct electrons and absorb light. Density-functional theory (DFT) computes them through costly self-consistent iterations, while existing machine-learning models either predict isolated scalar properties or output Hamiltonians that still require DFT solvers. Here we present EpNet, a learned empirical pseudopotential for crystals spanning 63 elements across the s, p and d blocks. An equivariant neural network builds its Hamiltonian from physics-motivated local potentials and nonlocal projectors. Trained solely on band energies, EpNet predicts complete band structures directly from atomic coordinates. On unseen chemical systems, its median errors are winAll eV for band energies and gapAll eV for band gaps. On 600,000 structures from an independent database, its band-gap errors are overall less than half those of existing models, at about 1% of DFT cost. EpNet thus enables fast screening of electronic properties for materials discovery and electronic-structure simulations of large systems.

title: An Extensible Agentic Framework for Expert-Level Automation of Atomistic Simulations
title_zh: 文献研究：An Extensible Agentic Framework for Expert-Level Automation of Atomistic Simulations
summary: Traditionally, atomistic simulation has been constrained by the computational scaling limits of ab initio methods and the parameterization overhead of empirical force fields. The recent emergence of u…
abstract: arXiv:2606.09422v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Traditionally, atomistic simulation has been constrained by the computational scaling limits of ab initio methods and the parameterization overhead of empirical force fields. The recent emergence of universal machine learning interatomic potentials has significantly mitigated these bottlenecks, offering near-quantum accuracy and generalizability across diverse chemical spaces at a fraction of the computational cost. However, this shift has relocated the bottleneck to the human dimension: time-consuming mechanical processes, such as input preparation and data analysis, now dominate the research lifecycle. We introduce Paimon, a Platform for Agentic Integration in Materials Optimization and Nanoscale-simulations. Through hundreds of trials on an expert-level liquid electrolyte simulation, we show that Paimon substantially improves the reliability of agentic workflows by suppressing silent errors: plausible yet physically incorrect results. Paimon accommodates a new capability without modifying the agents already present, which we demonstrate by integrating an externally developed scientific agent. As an agent harness for atomistic simulations, Paimon affords researchers a continuous, science-centric workflow throughout the entire simulation lifecycle.

title: SATE: Transferable Spin-Adapted Neural Wavefunctions
title_zh: 文献研究：SATE: Transferable Spin-Adapted Neural Wavefunctions
summary: Accurate prediction of molecular reactivity requires both accurate and computationally efficient description of electron correlation and spin across various molecular geometries and electronic states.…
abstract: arXiv:2611.12002v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate prediction of molecular reactivity requires both accurate and computationally efficient description of electron correlation and spin across various molecular geometries and electronic states. We introduce SATE, a spin-adapted transferable neural wavefunction architecture with effective core potentials. SATE combines a transferable neural wavefunction, the spin-adapted antisymmetrization method, and effective core potentials into a single foundation model architecture pretrained on compositions containing selected elements from hydrogen to bromine. After pretraining and adaptation, our model is able to predict 3d transition-metal spin-state gaps, bond dissociation energies, and reaction energies by addressing two key issues. First, including the core potentials into the model allows us to reduce the number of explicitly treated electrons. Second, using spin-adapted antisymmetrization enforces the prescribed total spin by construction. By testing our model with 3d transition metal chemistry, we evaluate our model's description of strong electron correlation and competing electronic states in such compounds. We find that pretraining improves most tested component energies at matched adaptation budgets, while improvements in spin-state gaps, dissociation energies, and reaction energies remain system dependent. Ultimately, our work lays the foundation for more accurate and transferable modeling of molecular systems by combining the computational efficiency of effective core potentials with explicit control over total spin.
